diagnosis_explanation: Your cervix has cancer. This cancer is very small. It has not grown much. Doctors call this microinvasive carcinoma. We will talk about how to treat this.
medication_rationale:
Vicodin:
This medicine is a pain reliever. It can help manage any pain you have. You may feel sleepy or a bit dizzy at first. This should pass as your body gets used to it. Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing or feel very confused.

Motrin:
This medicine helps reduce pain and swelling. It is used to help with your urinary tract infection. You might notice some stomach upset. Taking it with food can help prevent this. Call your doctor if you have black or bloody stools, or if you have chest pain.

Macrodantin every night at bedtime:
This medicine fights germs that cause urinary tract infections. It helps keep your urinary tract healthy. You may notice your urine turns a darker yellow or brown color. This is a normal side effect. Call your doctor if you have a fever, chills, or a rash.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will likely feel tired and sore. This is normal.
- Rest is important. Avoid all heavy lifting.
- You may have some light vaginal bleeding. This is normal.
- Call your doctor if you have heavy bleeding.
- Call your doctor if you have a fever over 100.4 F.
- Your goal this week is to walk short distances inside your home.

**Week 2:**
- Your energy may start to slowly return.
- You can do light activities around the house.
- Avoid lifting anything heavier than 5 pounds.
- Avoid sexual activity.
- Call your doctor if you have bad pelvic pain.
- Your goal this week is to walk a little longer each day.

**Week 3:**
- You may feel less pain and more comfort.
- You can try slightly longer walks.
- Continue to avoid heavy lifting or strenuous exercise.
- You can start to do very light household chores.
- Call your doctor if you see pus from the incision.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 10 minutes without stopping.

**Week 4:**
- You should notice steady improvement in how you feel.
- You can increase your walking distance slowly.
- Keep avoiding heavy lifting for now.
- Discuss returning to work with your doctor.
- Your goal this week is to walk outside daily.
- Call your doctor if you have any new or worsening pain.

**When to expect improvement:**
- You should feel much better over the next 4 weeks.
- Healing takes time. Be patient with yourself.
- Attend all follow-up appointments.
- Continue to follow your doctor's instructions.
